source: Christchurch City Council, District Plan Tree Protection (Appendix 9.4.7.1 schedule of significant trees), joined to the CCC Tree asset layer for species and size
join_endpoint: https://gis.ccc.govt.nz/server/rest/services/OpenData/Tree/FeatureServer/0/query (TreeID = TreeSpecimenID; species, ownership, DBH, height, crown spread)
licence_proof: ArcGIS item 4ba27f529fd34359b465e7492a15bb77 (DP Tree Protection (OpenData)) and item 0c557c04453e435ba1e50389db0ede90 (Tree (OpenData)), licenseInfo verbatim on both: "CCC - Open Data - Use of this dataset is permitted in accordance with the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) License https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/". The ArcGIS Hub dataset API returns structuredLicense type CC-BY-4.0 for the protection layer. Read 2026-09-24.
designation: District Plan scheduled tree. The layer description: "a tree specimen that is deemed worthy of preservation in the District Plan due to its scenic, recreational, scientific, historical and or other value. (It is commonly referred to as a Heritage or Notable tree)." All records LegalStatus Operative.
scope: Every scheduled point in the layer (Scheduled Significant Tree, Scheduled Tree Group, Scheduled Park Tree Group, Scheduled Street Tree Group), covering Christchurch city and Banks Peninsula. Filtered: points whose specimen record says Ownership Private are DROPPED (hard rule 10), as are specimens no longer ServiceStatus Current. Group categories are individual tree points belonging to a scheduled group; a group is usually not a collectible point, so treat Scheduled Significant Tree as the primary candidates.
caveat: dbh_m is the CCC field DiameterAtBreastHeight, which reads as METRES (2.76 for a Wellingtonia of 35 m); girth_cm is derived as pi x dbh and only where dbh is between 0.05 and 6 m. Check units against the physical tree before quoting. location_certainty often reads "Approximate XY", so every dot defaults to approximate. Ownership values other than Private (Council, Crown, unknown) are kept; a null ownership is not proof of public access. No vitality beyond ServiceStatus Current.
